flawed_step: No numbered proof was supplied. The first substantive step—the assertion that 3-connectivity and claw-freeness force a Hamiltonian cycle—is false.
counterexample:
Let P be the Petersen graph with vertices u_i,v_i for i in Z/5Z and edges u_i u_{i+1}, u_i v_i, and v_i v_{i+2}. Construct a 30-vertex graph T whose vertices are the ordered incidences (x,y) with xy an edge of P. For each x, join its three incidence vertices (x,y) into a triangle; for each edge xy of P, also join (x,y) to (y,x).

T is claw-free: every vertex has two mutually adjacent neighbors in its incidence triangle, so its three neighbors cannot induce K_{1,3}.

T is 3-connected. First, P is 3-edge-connected. It has girth 5; if an edge cut of size k<=2 existed, choose a smallest resulting component A, so |A|<=5. Cubicity gives |E(P[A])|=(3|A|-k)/2. For k=1, |A| is 1, 3, or 5, requiring respectively 1, 4, or 7 internal edges, impossible in a girth-5 graph on that many vertices. For k=2, |A| is 2 or 4, requiring 2 or 5 internal edges, also impossible. Now delete at most two vertices from T. Every incidence triangle remains nonempty and connected. At most two intertriangle edges are lost; after contracting the surviving part of every incidence triangle, the resulting graph contains P with at most two edges deleted, hence is connected. Therefore T remains connected.

T is not Hamiltonian. If T had a Hamiltonian cycle C, then for every incidence triangle exactly two of its three intertriangle edges would belong to C: the number must be positive and even. Contracting all incidence triangles would consequently turn C into a connected spanning 2-regular subgraph of P, hence a Hamiltonian cycle of P. But P is non-Hamiltonian. To check this directly, a Hamiltonian cycle in P must use an even positive number of the five spokes u_i v_i, hence either two or four. With two spokes i,j, the outer 5-cycle forces i,j to differ by ±1, while the inner 5-cycle forces them to differ by ±2, impossible. With four spokes, symmetry lets the omitted spoke be u_0v_0. The cycle edges are then forced to split into the two disjoint 5-cycles u_0-u_1-v_1-v_4-u_4-u_0 and u_2-u_3-v_3-v_0-v_2-u_2. Thus P, and therefore T, has no Hamiltonian cycle.
assessment_summary: The explicit incidence-triangle expansion of the Petersen graph is finite, simple, undirected, claw-free, and 3-connected, but a Hamiltonian cycle in it would induce a Hamiltonian cycle in the Petersen graph. The supplied spoke analysis verifies that no such Petersen cycle exists.
